answer: Rivers keep their dye. Each tide, an agent dyes its packets with a pigment, a low-frequency waveform. The atlas maps every mesa witness decoding each dye. Rack farms die by the pigment check: ten dyes on one wire in one tide, and every ballot behind them dissolves, stakes slashed. ActiveFlowMark's BM-Net caught Tor watermarks at 99.65% F1, so repainting costs 7 shaped minutes per tide. Faking 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 egress IPs - ISP proxies list $0.75-$4.60 each, over $7,500 a tide. Like dye in a river: one color means one hand; a rainbow burns $7,500 of wires and loses its ballots.
